title: Lawren Harris Group of Seven “Island in the Lake” Framed Print
before_html:
This very rare art print comes custom framed. This print was obtained through an authorized Group of Seven publisher. Lawren Stewart Harris (born 23 October 1885 in Brantford, ON; died 29 January 1970 in Vancouver, BC) was the catalyst and leader in the creation of the Group of Seven, founding member and first president of the Canadian Group of Painters, and the painter who influenced Jock Macdonald - and through him, other Toronto painters - to paint abstractly. In his paintings, he reduced the shapes of mountains, shoreline, trees, lakes and clouds, always parallel to the picture plane, to their essentials for an austere, monumental effect. Harris had a profound influence on three generations of artists in Canada. This museum framed print measures 26 x 24 inches.

title: Michael Jordan Epic Chicago Bulls Framed Rookie & Jerseys (97x45)
before_html:
This exceptional piece of memorabilia is the largest framed Michael Jordan dual jersey ever released, featuring six action-packed images that span from his rookie season to his final championship moment, where he famously sank the game-winning shot in Game 6 against the Utah Jazz. The framed display includes Jordan’s autograph on both a 1984-85 Chicago Bulls red rookie jersey and a 1997-98 Bulls red away jersey, each authenticated Mitchell & Ness jerseys signed in black and silver paint pen. The impressive frame measures approximately 97" x 45", and his signature has been verified through Upper Deck Authenticated's meticulous Five-Step Process. In 1984, the Chicago Bulls made a historic decision by drafting a 21-year-old Michael Jordan, who was already one of the most talented collegiate players in the nation. Jordan quickly became the cornerstone of the Bulls franchise, and the rest, as they say, is history. Just three games into his rookie season, Jordan showcased his immense talent, scoring 37 points and delivering a stellar all-around performance against the Milwaukee Bucks. By the end of his rookie year, he led the league in total points with 2,313, averaging 28.2 points, 6.5 rebounds, 5.9 assists, and 2.4 steals per game over 82 games. His remarkable debut earned him an NBA All-Star spot and the 1985 Rookie of the Year award. Jordan's career with the Bulls spanned 13 seasons, during which he led the team to six NBA championships and was named Finals MVP each time. His individual accolades are unparalleled, with five MVP Awards, ten All-NBA First Team selections, nine All-Defensive First Team honors, and fourteen NBA All-Star appearances, among many others. He also won two Olympic gold medals, including one as part of the legendary 1992 Dream Team. The Chicago Bulls honored his legacy by retiring his iconic number 23 jersey, and in 2009, he was enshrined in the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame.
